facts.fact: A novel statistical singing voice conversion (SVC) technique with direct waveform modification based on the spectrum differential is presented.
facts.supporting_span: This paper presents a novel statistical singing voice conversion (SVC) technique with direct waveform modification based on the spectrum differential

facts.fact: The singing voice conversion technique can convert voice timbre of a source singer into that of a target singer.

facts.fact: The singing voice conversion technique does not use a vocoder to generate converted singing voice waveforms.

facts.fact: SVC makes it possible to convert singing voice characteristics of an arbitrary source singer into those of an arbitrary target singer.

facts.fact: Speech quality of the converted singing voice is significantly degraded compared to that of a natural singing voice.

facts.fact: The speech quality degradation is due to various factors, such as analysis and modeling errors in the vocoder-based framework.

facts.fact: A statistical conversion process is proposed to alleviate degradation.

facts.fact: The statistical conversion process directly modifies the signal in the waveform domain.

facts.fact: The statistical conversion process estimates the difference in the spectra of the source and target singers' singing voices.

facts.fact: The differential spectral feature is directly estimated using a differential Gaussian mixture model (GMM).
